sections.text: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।
That which is not, shall never be; that which is, shall never cease to be. To the wise, these truths are self-evident.
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।
The Spirit, which pervades all that we see, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy the Spirit.
The material bodies which this Eternal, Indestructible, Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite. Therefore fight, O Valiant Man!

So we had been discussing Chapter 2, Sankhya Yoga, Yoga of Knowledge. This is the knowledge about our true self. So verse 11 through 30 give us the Upanishaddic definition of what the self is all about. So Bhagawan starts with telling Arjuna that you should start looking at this world very differently. It is something like for any corporate planning there is short term planning and a long term planning. So there are some things you have to look at it from short term planning.
You have to get these things done during this quarter, but then you also have to look at it on a long term basis what will be in next 10 years. So Bhagavan says that right now we are looking at the world from a very short narrow perspective which is limited to this life. But this life is not the end by itself. This life is nothing but just a fraction of your own existence. So he starts with saying, you are worrying about these people. They are not worth worrying about.
No relatives of yours or friend of yours you should worry about whether he is dead or alive. It was a very shocking declaration to Arjuna, why shouldnt I be worrying about my own kith and kin? When you look at it from this narrow perspective, it will seem that something is good or bad. But we have learned that good and bad is a relative perspective. So what is maybe good in a short term may not be good in a long term. Thats why we have come across two terms.
Prayas is pleasant temporarily. Shreyas is good forever. That which is always good is Shreyas. That which is temporarily pleasant is Prayas. So the situation I see may be pleasant for now -- from Arjunas point of view, running away from this battle is pleasant. Less things to worry about, but its not pleasant in the long run.
You can allow these criminals to continue doing their crimes and this non Aryan like behavior, as Krishna puts it, the way these people are behaving is not fit to be an Aryan. Therefore to establish Dharma of Arya Bhart, it is your duty as the Kshatriya to fight this war. Thats basically Krishnas message here. So he said, you shouldnt be worrying about them. But then he starts from the widest perspective saying the existence for any being is eternal. We are eternal beings.
There was never a time where you were not there, or I was not there, or these kings were not there. So we are all eternal beings, immortal beings. We consider ourselves to be mortal. So thats basically the paradigm shift for Arjuna and all of us. How to look at our life. There will be a narrow perspective.
There is a relative reality. When there is a ice cube in my glass, it has this relative reality. The ice cube is very solid. But if I wait long enough, that ice cube will be gone. There will be just water. Water relatively has a longer existence than ice cube.
Ice cube is a very short term existence. I, as an intelligent being who use ice before, I know that that if I really want to use this ice, I have to use it as quickly as possible. Otherwise the ice will go away. There wont be any ice. So if I want to say you have to look at this situation from a wider perspective, that these people cannot be killed. And therefore he said, just as they have progressed from one existence to another, you have progressed one existence to another in your life.
From a childhood to adulthood and to old age, you will also migrate to the new state of existence. Deha Antara -- transferring from one body to another -- will not be any different from your migration from childhood to adulthood. Therefore, wise person who has understood this fundamental truth will not get confused. One who has understood the widest perspective of existence, he will not be worried about a small change in existence. When you understand water and ice, and the ice becomes water, you dont get upset.
Maybe you have to put it back into the freezer if you want more ice in the ice cube tray. So we know that the existence is permanent. Bhagavan says, but there may be a temporary consequences of me dealing with this world. Those experiences in my life create Sukha and Dukha. Matraha Sparsaha Tu Kaunteya -- When sense organs come in contact with sense objects, it will create an experience.
That experience, depending on the qualities of your sense organs, will be either pleasant or unpleasant. One experience which is pleasant to me may be unpleasant to somebody else. Jumping from 50ft on a bungee jumping is pleasant to somebody. It will not be pleasant for me. Same experience can give two different experiences to two different people in the same set of circumstances. Depending on his own equipment, depending on my mind if it is rainy outside it may be unpleasant.
But if Im a farmer or a gardener, it may be a pleasant experience. The bhagawan said, matrahas parsaha tu kunteya sita ushna sukh dukadah. They give these experiences of sukhendukha. They are nothing but perceptions of your mind. And therefore he said, taam titiksha bharad. You have no other choice.
Whether its pleasant or unpleasant, you must bear them. Know that they are temporary. They have beginning and an end. And therefore, even a pleasant experience -- dont get too excited or too elated, because it will also come to an end. Every other day we hear about recession and then the next day we hear about no, no, the market is going to keep going.
How long? We know for sure there will be a recession sometime. We just hope it will not be before I retire, thats all. So every experience has a beginning and end. While we are experiencing, if we remember that, that this is a temporary experience, we will not get too invested in that experience. We get too invested in their experience. Thats where we get either too excited or elated or too depressed.
The right way to live is to bear them all -- pleasant and unpleasant. And then Bhagavan now defines what is the nature of the self. So other day I also had a new revelation about the ownership of this building. So my condo administrator came to me as a Krishna to explain to me what I own and what I dont own. We obviously all of you know that Meena and I own this building. So we always say, well, we own this building.
Everything outside parking lot is common area. We own this building. There was clear understanding the last about 14 years we owned this building or 16 years we owned this building. The other day we had a water damage. Hot water heater broke and it was just spraying out water all over the bathroom. So I had to obviously call.
I actually called fire department because I didnt know what to do. By the time fire department came, the guy who was cleaning the carpet, he figured out there is a shut off valve outside. He shut it off, everything was fine. But when I reported it to our condo guy, he said, well, Ill come down Rajan and check it out whether theres any damage in the attic. He walked through my attic. He found that we were storing old drawings and files in our attic.
We have storage trusses. He said, Rajan, I dont want to be a pain in your neck, but youre not supposed to store anything in an attic. He said, why is that? He said, because you only own building from your ceiling to the top of the floor. The attic does not belong to you. I said, who owns the attic? He said, the condo association.
I said, are you serious? They say, yeah, yeah, you only own from the ceiling to the floor. They said, what about below the floor? He said, that also condo association. He said, what about outside? He said, you only went from the inside face of your exterior wall to the other side interior face of exterior wall.
I said, who owns the exterior walls? The condo association. So I said, who owns the building? He said, Rajan, you own the space within the exterior walls, the ceiling, and the floor. I said, so nothing concrete which I can call a building is mine? He said, no, none of that is yours.
You as a condo owner only own the space. Do you mean to say the condo association tomorrow can decide that they want to take the roof away because they own the roof and then they take the four walls away? Yeah, technically they own. Now, how about the ground below? They own the ground below too. All you own is space within four walls, floor and a ceiling.
They say, okay, you try to remove that. Ill tell you, demarcate my space from outside space, inside space, because my condo is just the space. You can remove floors, wall and ceiling as condo owner association. You wont be able to take this space away because I own this space. Now, thats a completely different way to look at this condo ownership. First of all, the bank has the mortgage on this space, so I owe them money. And when I want to sell something, I only own the space. There is nothing tangible which I can say I own outright. But technically, free and clear, what I own is just the space inside this building. Even though it has no value by itself -- without the walls, floor and ceiling, the space has no practical meaning. The space is defining the value of the conditioning, but the conditionings are defining the limitations of the space.
Bhagavan said to Arjuna that you have to start looking at your relationship to your teacher and your grandfather in a very different way. And therefore he says, avinasi tu tadviddhi en sarvam idam tatham. So what is my relationship with that self which is residing in all these beings? If all these beings are immortal, but they can get killed. What is getting killed and what is immortal? So Bhagavan now defines the relationship between the perishable and imperishable.
The Imperishable is the one which is the essence of any being. Any being is called a being as long as the consciousness is functioning through him. I am who I am as long as Im alive. Without that consciousness, it is nothing but a dead body. The dead body is not Rajan Mehta. But he said that which you call your relative Bhishma and Drona.
That essence is Avinashi. It cannot be destroyed. Tadvidi, know that the essence of a being with whom you have a relationship with is indestructible. It is not limited to that person. This is a complete paradigm shift for most of us who have never thought about it. I have always thought that my self is residing in me and your self is residing in you and herself is residing in her.
Theyre all kind of nice little packages of selves, you know. And we are interacting with each other. That which makes your friend your friend is actually indestructible. Your cousin, your cousin is indestructible. Your teacher, teacher indestructible. But that essence is not limited to him.
Everything is pervaded by that essence which you call yourself, which you call your friends self, which you call grandfathers self. Anything that you can think of, anything they can perceive. Your world perception may be as grand as the entire universe. Anything that you can think of in a sarvam idam tatham, it is all pervaded by that self.

These verses contain one of the Gitas most essential teachings: That which is not, shall never be; that which is, shall never cease to be. This distinguishes between the Real (Sat) and the Unreal (Asat). The Real is that which exists in all three periods of time - past, present, and future - without any change. The Unreal is that which appears to exist but has no permanent reality, like a snake seen in a rope or ice that melts into water. The body and all material forms belong to this changing, temporary reality.
Verse 17 declares: The Spirit, which pervades all that we see, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy the Spirit. This all-pervading Spirit is not limited to your body or mine - it is the same consciousness expressing through all beings, like electricity manifesting as light, heat, and sound through different appliances. Therefore, Krishna concludes in verse 18: The material bodies which this Eternal, Indestructible, Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite. Therefore fight, O Valiant Man!
Apply this teaching today by examining what you consider real in your life. Your possessions, relationships, status, body - which of these will exist unchanged forever? Now consider: What remains constant through all the changes of your life? That unchanging awareness is your true Self. When you feel threatened or anxious, ask: Is it the Real or the Unreal that is threatened? The Real cannot be harmed; the Unreal was never truly yours to lose. How does this shift your perspective on what you fear losing?
